messages:
akira: FYI rolling kernel-selector v2.2 to canary caused a subtle host-side regression: ingress p99 increased 38ms -> 67ms and sys CPU up ~18%. noticed after a burst of short requests.
liz: thanks for the flag. i pulled traces and flamegraphs shows a lot of tiny http2 DATA frames being writev'd from tokenizer -> proxy -> kernel.
oliver: kvcache graphs show increased async-writes and index churn around the same time. looks like more tiny fragments are hitting the hot shard and causing backpressure.
akira: repro gist from ferry logs (sanitized):
```
[ingress] recv req
tokenizer: emit 48b buffer
proxy: writev({hdr,48b,ctl}) -> flush
kernel: sys_writev(3) -> return
```
akira: before v2.2 these were coalesced in proxy into one 1kb write, now they go as many small syscalls.
sam: kernel-selector v2.2 biases the low-latency kernel which reduced allowed batching window. that aligns with the change.
liz: flame link: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/3129994444 ; shows syscall hotpath dominated.
perf-bot: nightly perf diff: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/9001/diffs/3129994444 (regression flagged)
oliver: short-term mitigation: enable proxy feature ingress.adaptive_coalesce=true which buffers small frames for up to 8ms and coalesces by origin_stream. that should cut writev count and reduce kvcache churn.
akira: quick canary plan: flip adaptive_coalesce on 10% canary at 3129994500, monitor ingress_p99, sys_cpu, kvcache_hot_evictions for 15m. roll back criteria: p99 > 75ms or error% increase > 0.3%.
sam: long-term we should teach kernel-selector to expose a "write-density" hint so it prefers kernels that tolerate slightly larger batching windows when ingress writev rate > X.
liz: experiment results from local bench: adaptive_coalesce=true -> writev calls -72%, ingress_p99 -> 44ms (from 67ms), kvcache evict rate -40%. added microbench numbers to PR.
akira: tagging @sam to follow up on kernel-selector hinting; @oliver to add a kvcache alert for hot-shard-evict-rate > 4/s during canary.
oliver: on it. setting alert and dashboard tiles.
akira: rolling now. will paste rollback steps in the incidents channel and attach the perf snapshots after 10m.
